You are an adversarial verifier for a proposed STRUCTURAL refactor in the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim.
READ-ONLY: do not edit, build, or run anything. Use Read/Grep/Glob only.

Claim (from reviewer driver-profile):
- file: driver/cmd_profile.cpp:216
- category: duplication
- title: Third hand-rolled mkdtemp scratch-dir implementation; also hardcodes /tmp unlike the other two
- detail: The driver has three mkdtemp implementations: tempdir.cpp:11-18 make_temp_dir() (fs::temp_directory_path + prefix-XXXXXX, the designated shared helper per tempdir.hpp:1-2), run_plan.cpp:368-379 (inline temp_directory_path + "andesim-plan-XXXXXX" + mkdtemp), and cmd_profile.cpp:216-231 (struct Workdir with the literal template "/tmp/andesim-profile.XXXXXX"). cmd_profile's copy is the only one that hardcodes /tmp, ignoring $TMPDIR, and tempdir.hpp's comment ('currently: --runtime linux's manifest staging') documents that the shared helper has only one consumer while two near-copies exist. Workdir's RAII remove_all is 3 lines on top of make_temp_dir(); run_plan already does its own remove_all at line 453.
- claimed safety: Replacing both open-coded sites with make_temp_dir() keeps the same create-unique-dir semantics and each caller's existing cleanup. The only observable delta is cmd_profile's workdir moving from a hardcoded /tmp to the system temp dir (identical when $TMPDIR is unset, which is the tested configuration); no test asserts the /tmp prefix - test_andes_sim_profile.sh greps the staged cfg as '-readconfig .*/qemu\.cfg', path-agnostic. Update tempdir.hpp's 'currently:' comment in the same commit so it does not go stale.

Try to REFUTE it. For dead-code: grep the WHOLE repo (and the demo suite at /home/nick/work/andesim-demo, and consider that vsim lives in a separate repo /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim - grep there too if the symbol could cross repos) for references. For duplication: read both sites fully and check they really are behavior-identical. For stale-doc: read the doc AND the code it describes. For bug-report: check whether the behavior is actually wrong vs intended. If the change could alter ANY observable behavior (output text, exit codes, file layout, test expectations), verdict RISKY with the exact risk. If the claim is wrong, REJECTED. Only CONFIRMED when you verified the evidence yourself.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# `andesim profile` contract: hot inner-loop detection rides the engine's own
3	# QEMU config. Like hybrid, profile picks a cycle-accurate engine (--engine or
4	# the sole one) and derives the QEMU launch from it: -cpu from the engine's
5	# `--print-qemu-config` driver globals, vlen from its --describe, the staged
6	# qemu.cfg as -readconfig. Layers:
7	#
8	#   1. unit (fast, pure): the profile core (parse/filter/nest/render/argv)
9	#      plus the CLI parse of the profile flags.
10	#   2. fake engines (no real vsim, no QEMU): throwaway engine scripts that
11	#      answer --describe AND --print-qemu-config drive the real
12	#      discover -> resolve -> probe -> argv path; --dry-run prints the exact
13	#      QEMU command without spawning it, so every assertion is deterministic.
14	#   3. real engine (guarded): the probe/argv against a built sim_* binary,
15	#      still --dry-run (the full QEMU run is covered by
16	#      tests/plugin/test_plugin_hotIterationLoop_measure.sh).
17	set -uo pipefail
18	
19	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
20	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
21	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
22	
23	BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
24	
25	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
26	
27	# 1. unit: profile core + CLI parse
28	"$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-profile-test" || fail "profile unit tests failed"
29	"$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-cli-test" || fail "cli unit tests failed"
30	
31	# --- fixtures: throwaway engine scripts in a scanned dir --------------------
32	TMP=$(mktemp -d)
33	trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
34	
35	# mkengine DIR FILE ID VLEN CPU: a fake cycle-accurate engine whose
36	# --print-qemu-config names CPU (a minimal but valid -readconfig text). An
37	# empty CPU makes the probe FAIL (exit 1), like an engine without the hook.
38	mkengine() {
39	  local f="$1/$2"
40	  cat >"$f" <<EOF
41	#!/bin/sh
42	if [ "\$1" = "--describe" ]; then
43	  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$3","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","xlen":64,"vlen":$4,"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]}}'
44	elif [ "\$1" = "--print-qemu-config" ]; then
45	  [ -n "$5" ] || exit 1
46	  printf '[global]\ndriver = "$5-riscv-cpu"\nproperty = "vlen"\nvalue = "$4"\n'
47	else
48	  echo "RAN:\$*"
49	fi
50	EOF
51	  chmod +x "$f"
52	}
53	
54	D1="$TMP/one"; D2="$TMP/two"; DE="$TMP/empty"; DN="$TMP/nocfg"
55	mkdir -p "$D1" "$D2" "$DE" "$DN"
56	mkengine "$D1" v1 "vsim:v1" 256 "andes-ax45mpv"
57	mkengine "$D2" v1 "vsim:v1" 512 "andes-ax45mpv"
58	mkengine "$D2" v2 "vsim:v2" 128 "andes-ax66"
59	mkengine "$DN" v1 "vsim:v1" 512 ""   # probe fails -> default -cpu, no -readconfig
60	
61	DUMMY="$TMP/dummy.elf"; : >"$DUMMY"
62	
63	# 2a. sole engine is the default; the dry-run shows the full QEMU command with
64	# the engine-derived -cpu (model from the probe, vlen from --describe), the
65	# staged -readconfig, the plugin with default limit/min_iters, and -bios.
66	# One spawn, grepped per assertion (each run pays discovery + probe spawns).
67	out=$(env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
68	[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "2a dry-run: rc=$rc: $out"
69	for re in \
70	  '\-plugin .*libhotIterationLoop\.so,limit=50,min_iters=1' \
71	  '\-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=256' \
72	  '\-readconfig .*/qemu\.cfg' \
